required_changes.change: Add one explicit native process-control selection and immutable prepared contract reference for the selected Python. Pin the provider helper, actual selected executable inode and bytes, ABI, public syscall headers and actual libc image and symbol offsets. Keep absent/default selection on the unchanged Python API path. Never infer selection from missing exports.

Include linux_pidfd_process_control.py only when the plan explicitly selects it. Before any Nsight version, capture, export or other tool spawn, construct one producer-owned NativePidfdProvider from exact declared bytes and complete self open/signal-zero/close preflight. Reuse that same provider through NativeProcessObserver in the closed descendant scope and positive ancestry checks. Do not instantiate a new provider on every generic reader call or overwrite os/signal APIs.

Publish exact provider contract, bootstrap, actual preflight and complete bounded native call records joined to the actual producer PID/birth/UID/cgroup, plan and source. Add a pure saved-evidence reader that checks calls, descriptor identity, ordinary and reserved operation budgets, waits and no remaining handles without making native calls during audit. Require these records for the explicit native path; refuse missing, substituted, duplicate or incomplete records. Retain historical default API readers explicitly.

Prepare a fresh zero-environment diagnostic under selected Python on the approved target. Require actual trusted process/source/tool identity, sole-producer lock custody, subreaper and complete descendant waits/cleanup with native handle evidence. Review actual raw records independently before any separate profiling admission. CPU provider review grants no target or profiling admission.

Separately correct and review current common-helper prerequisite closure compatibility, then preserve every existing original numerical/configuration/seed/package/backend/schema-two image/physical UUID/PCI/minor/own-only sampling/correctness/performance gate. A zero-environment process test does not replace actual current CUDA and mapped backend qualification or authorize ordinary profiles.
